_plate: art-source/level10/map_level10.png at 3840x2160, encoded to public/assets/maps/map_level10.webp at q95 and registered in art.json as `map-level10`, with `map.level10` pointing at it.
_roadWidth: 44.5, the median lane width measured by tools/trace_level10.py by casting normals along the centreline, and re-measured independently by tools/check_level10.py. The band is 44.5 px over most of its length and widens at the hairpins, which is the paint rather than the measurement -- the sampled range is 35.5 to 58.0.
note: AI OVERRIDE PART 2: the machine's core chamber. ONE continuous lane, in through the west housing at 47.2% of the height and out through the east housing at 47.8%, over a field of hex floor plating, with the cracked purple crystal core in the upper right. NO FORKS AND NO ALTERNATE ROUTES -- the painted band encloses no region at all, which is the check that found level 9's fork, run here and come back empty. Route switching was cut from the design and there is nothing in this plate to switch between.
_spotRadius: 34, every other level's. World 1280 renders to 844 CSS px, so 34 world px is a 44.8 px tap diameter and anything under 44 pt is smaller than a thumb.
_waypoints: ONE LANE, 104 traced points plus TWO computed ones: a gateway at x=-60.0 and a vanish point at x=1340.0, each extended along the heading the lane already has at its terminal so enemies walk in and out along the paint. THE PAINTED LANE DOES NOT REACH EITHER FRAME EDGE: a piece of machine housing is drawn over it at each end and the cyan re-emerges as a stub at the frame, so tools/trace_level10.py bridges the two housings before it walks the geodesic. Painted length 3309.8 px; walked with the two computed points 3440.1.
_buildSpots: 21 PADS, HAND-PLACED. They come from tools/plots.json by way of tools/apply_plots.py and they replace the 12 the scoring pass chose -- levels 3, 4 and 8's sweep, run here with its constants unchanged: a radius-24 core on painted plating, 90-114 px from the centreline, 74 px apart, best-first by uncovered lane. THAT BAND IS NOT A CONSTRAINT ON THIS SET and the numbers say so: standoff 53.6-146.3. NOT LEVEL 9's ONE-PAD-PER-PAINTED-CHIP either, and the reason is in the art: level 9 painted fifteen chips of 81x75 median, so its buildable ground WAS those chips; level 10 paints eleven open panels up to 223x150, and one pad on one of those wastes it. They reach 94.9% of the lane at range 132 -- which is where the twelve were, because the sweep optimised for exactly this and a hand cannot beat it at its own game. WHAT THE NINE EXTRA PADS BUY IS DEPTH, not reach: more guns on the same road. The count per level is 10, 10, 14, 14, 18, 18, 17, 20, 15, 21, read out of each board's own source by tools/padcounts.py rather than typed: this is the BIGGEST board in the game now and it was the second-smallest, and Vlaude's health was soaked against the small one.
_hazardSpots: WHERE VLAUDE CAN GENERATE A WALL. Points ON the lane, at fixed fractions of walked route distance, so they survive a retrace at a different resolution. They are in the MAP rather than in level10.json because they are geometry -- level5.json's acid is in the rules because the boss drops it wherever it is standing, and these are authored positions on this road. The rules file says how many may stand at once and what a wall does; this says where.
_vlaudeBerth: WHERE VLAUDE IS PARKED FOR PHASES 1 AND 2, off the lane at the crystal core. Derived by tools/trace_level10.py rather than placed: the purple mask is dilated by 5 so the CRACKED crystal's facets merge, and the berth is the bounding box of every purple mass in the upper-right quadrant -- centre x, bottom y, so he stands in front of the core instead of inside it. 127.9 px from the lane centreline, which is further than any tower's range reaches, and he is untargetable in those phases regardless.
